frequency_question: How often do highly disruptive announced executive tariffs on major trading partners actually take effect within a short implementation window rather than being averted or delayed by negotiation?
membership_rule: Includes explicitly announced, high-magnitude import tariffs on specific allied nations or sectors where implementation was scheduled within 60 days. Excludes broad statutory anti-dumping/countervailing duties determined by administrative agencies.

cases.name: 2019 US-Mexico Tariff Threat over Border Security

coverage_note: 4 named instances representing direct bilateral tariff threats against integrated partners where implementation was initially scheduled within a tight timeframe.
known_gaps: Excludes minor sectoral threats that did not reach a formal presidential proclamation stage with a fixed deadline.
skeleton: Threatened bilateral trade escalations against close integrated neighbors within economic pacts (USMCA/NAFTA precursors)
multiplier: 2 hits out of 4 major threatened escalations against integrated partners
validity_reason: Valid for the duration of current executive trade policy tendencies regarding bilateral negotiations.
